messages:
IncidentBot: paging: high-error-rate detected on /v1/generate in hosted-usw2 (err rate > 8% over 2m). Paging oncall: @Emma (oncall). Incident ID ir-2134. Auto-allocated bridge #inc-2134.

Emma (oncall): ack. joining bridge now. quick hypothesis: weekend traffic pattern + model hot-shard? grabbing logs.

Sanjay R: also seeing a spike in 95th latency and 5xxs from the load-balancer side. pushing preliminary metrics to the incident dash.

Maria - Support: tagging for CS. If this hits the hosted API customers we'll need an initial customer-facing blurb. Can we confirm scope (embeddings vs generation)?

Emma (oncall): current scope: only text/generation route /v1/generate. embeddings endpoints look fine. impact: requests occasionally 500 or time out; retry reduces success rate but still failing for some customers. region: us-west-2 primarily.

Alex D: logs show OOM hits on model-worker-3 and elevated KV cache misses. suspect sudden cache churn from a large prefix-heavy workload.

Emma (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) scale model-workers + disable lazy-cache-eviction for 10m. 2) add temporary circuit-breaker at edge to reject >10s requests with 429. 3) post initial status page and CS template. doing #1 now (autoscale request).

SupportBot: autoscale request accepted: +4 workers queued for warmup (pool: dedicated-hosted-usw2). ETA ~90s.

Sanjay R: while workers warm up, can we push an immediate fallback policy to route new requests to a smaller model variant (latency/cost tradeoff) to reduce pressure? I can run rollback if quality issues appear.

Emma (oncall): good call. rolling out fallback route to model v2-small as canary for 10% of traffic. applying now.

Emma (oncall): DRAFT status page update (please proof):
```
Status: Degraded performance in US-WEST-2 affecting text generation (/v1/generate).
Impact: Some requests return 500 or time out; embeddings and other endpoints unaffected.
Start time: 2026-03-15T10:31:30Z
Customer impact: partial, user-facing latency and errors for generation calls in us-west-2.
Mitigation: Additional workers are being provisioned and a temporary fallback to a smaller model variant has been rolled out for a portion of traffic.
Next update: in 15 minutes or as significant progress occurs.
```

Maria - Support: LGTM. small tweak suggestion: add "workaround: retry with exponential backoff" line. Also prepare Zendesk/Intercom quick replies.

Emma (oncall): adding workaround line. final draft approved. posting now to status page.

SupportBot: statuspage update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/ir-2134 (public).

Maria - Support: Agent macro for Zendesk (copyable):
```
[Macro title] Generation endpoint partial outage - quick acknowledgement
[Macro body]
Hi {{customer.first_name}},

Thanks for the report — we're aware of an issue affecting generation requests in the US-WEST-2 region (some requests may return 500 or time out). Our engineers are provisioning additional capacity and we have a partial fallback in place to reduce errors.

Workaround: please retry requests with exponential backoff (recommended initial delay 250ms, max 4 retries).

We will provide another update within 15 minutes. Sorry for the disruption.

— Redwood Support
```

Maria - Support: Intercom quick snippet (short):
```
We’re investigating increased errors for text generation in US-WEST-2. Engineers are provisioning capacity and routing some traffic to a fallback model. Retry with backoff for best results. Updates shortly.
```

Sanjay R: internal comm for sales/CS/execs (short):
```
INCIDENT ir-2134: degradation affecting generation in US-WEST-2. Notable customers may see errors. Mitigation: +4 workers, 10% traffic routed to v2-small fallback. ETA to stable: ~30m pending warmup and cache stabilization. CS: use Zendesk macro above for inbound tickets. Reaches: Maria (CS lead). Will update every 15m.
```

Alex D: while warmup completes, run these quick checks (triage checklist):
1) worker health: `kubectl get pods -l app=model-worker -n inference`
2) OOM logs: `kubectl logs <pod> -n inference | grep -i oom`
3) model cache eviction rate: `redis-cli MONITOR` / check cache-miss metric `cache.miss.rate` in prometheus
4) LB error ratios: `rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests_total{status=~\"5..\"}[1m])`
5) trace sample: query X-Ray/tracing for 5xx span aggregation on /v1/generate

Emma (oncall): running checks now. quick findings: eviction rate high, OOMs on two pods, LB 5xx spike at 8.7%. Warmup progressing.

Sanjay R: fallback route is live on 10% traffic. early signs: error rate on routed requests dropped to 1.2% but some degraded quality reported in canary logs (acceptable for short-term mitigation).

Maria - Support: compiling a customer email template for impacted accounts (longer form):
```
Subject: Brief service disruption affecting generation in US-WEST-2
Hi {{account_owner.first_name}},

We wanted to let you know about a partial service disruption impacting text generation calls routed through our US-WEST-2 region. Some requests may have returned errors or experienced higher latency starting at 2026-03-15T10:31:30Z.

What we’re doing: we’ve provisioned additional inference workers and implemented a temporary fallback to a smaller model for a portion of traffic to reduce errors while we stabilize cache behavior.

Workaround: if your integration retries automatically, please ensure exponential backoff is enabled. If you need us to route your account to a different region temporarily, reply and we’ll assist.

Impact: partial; embeddings and other API surfaces are not affected. We’ll follow up with a post-incident summary when root cause is confirmed.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is inconvenient.

— Redwood Support
```

Emma (oncall): making internal note for postmortem: suspected cache eviction algorithm regression combined with bursty prefix-heavy workload. Collecting heap dumps and cache metrics. tagging Research/Inference for model-runtime analysis.

Alex D: capture: `pgrep -a model_worker && sudo gcore -o /tmp/cores/model_worker <pid>` for core dump if another OOM occurs (note: coordinate with SRE).

SupportBot: autoscale complete: +4 workers are up and healthy.

Emma (oncall): post-mitigation status: errors reduced to 1.5% in us-west-2, latency 95th reduced to baseline+30ms. leaving fallback in place for 30m then ramp down if stable.

Sanjay R: recommend follow-up actions for the runbook: 1) add a detection threshold for cache-eviction spikes, 2) add automated warmup for model shards during scaling, 3) tune eviction policy to reduce OOMs on heavy-prefix workloads.

Maria - Support: closing loop with CS: sending the drafted customer emails to top-impacted accounts now. Using Zendesk macro to reply to inbound tickets.

Emma (oncall): preparing handoff notes for next oncall (covering brought-up mitigations and outstanding tasks):
```
Handoff - Emma (oncall) -> Sanjay R (next):
- Incident ir-2134 started 2026-03-15T10:31:30Z
- Current state: degraded -> recovering; errors ~1.5% in US-WEST-2
- Mitigations applied: +4 workers, 10% fallback to v2-small, temporary 429 circuit-breaker for >10s
- Outstanding actions: collect heap/core dumps if OOMs reappear, coordinate postmortem and RCA, implement cache-eviction alerts
- Contact list: Maria (CS), Alex D (runtime), Research/Inference team alias
```

Sanjay R: taking over. thanks Emma. will continue monitoring and open a postmortem ticket with RCA owner.

Emma (oncall): thanks all — handing off to @Sanjay R. leaving notes in the incident board and will attach logs/heap dumps we captured.

SupportBot: incident ir-2134 transitioned to monitoring at 2026-03-15T10:44:10Z. Next automated update scheduled in 30 minutes.

Maria - Support: final agent checklist for handling customer replies: 1) use Zendesk macro, 2) escalate to CS lead if customer requests region move, 3) collect sample request_id and timestamp, 4) add to incident thread via internal note.

Alex D: post-incident reminder: create a small KCI (key corrective improvement) ticket to add a canary test for prefix-heavy workloads to prevent regression.

Emma (oncall): closed loop: I'll draft the postmortem outline and assign RCA owners. Thanks everyone for quick responses. :thumbsup:
